# Benchmark baseline of internal/bid on darwin/arm64 (targets T1.6.4 and T13).
#
# Taken on 2026-11-23 on the tree of the commit that carries this file, whose
# parent is 12845e37e3 (branch ubd128: the UBD kernel tuning, ubdlevel 3 and
# the formatting work), with
#   go test -c -o bid.test internal/bid
#   ./bid.test -test.run XXX -test.bench BenchmarkKernel -test.benchmem \
#       -test.count 8 -test.benchtime 100ms
# in the directory src/internal/bid, and the lines below are that output
# unedited. The file is in benchstat form; compare a later run with
#   benchstat testdata/bench_baseline_darwin_arm64.txt new.txt
#
# Machine: 12-core Apple M3 Pro (6 performance, 6 efficiency cores) under
# macOS 26.6, with no other builds or benchmarks running. Load average
# (uptime, 1, 5 and 15 minutes) was 2.63 6.86 5.84 at the start of the run
# (13:02 EST) and 3.20 4.52 5.05 at its end (13:07).
#
# This replaces the baselines taken on a 16-core Apple M4 Max (2026-11-11 to
# 2026-11-16), which are in this file's git history. Three rows the branch
# added (ShortForm/128/short, PutLongFixed/128/long, IsShortFixed/128/mixed)
# had no sample there and the M4 Max was not available to retake it, so the
# whole file was retaken on this machine. A run on the M4 Max, the faster
# machine, reads every row under these figures: the ratchet logs such rows
# and does not fail them, so it bounds that machine only loosely.
#
# Rows are Op/Width/Class. Width 64 and 128 are the decimal kernel; float64 is
# the reference row, where the language has a counterpart. Every row includes
# a loop floor of about 0.3 ns (the float64 add row is nearly all floor).
#
# The ratchet is TestBenchRatchet, opt-in:
#   go test -run TestBenchRatchet internal/bid -args -bid.ratchet
# It measures each row in short runs and takes the smallest time, as it does
# for the samples below. A row fails when its time is over
#   baseline * (1 + ratchet-band) + ratchet-slack-ns
# or when it allocates. The band is 10%, as for the M4 Max baselines: the
# background load of a working machine moves sub-5-ns rows by a few percent
# between runs. The slack stands for the timer resolution on rows of about a
# nanosecond. The baseline moves only by a deliberate commit that replaces
# this file.
#
# ratchet-band: 0.10
# ratchet-slack-ns: 0.5
#
# linux/amd64: not recorded here. Its baseline is the file
# testdata/bench_baseline_linux_amd64.txt, taken by the CI of that platform;
# the ratchet skips a platform with no file.
#
goos: darwin
goarch: arm64
pkg: internal/bid
cpu: Apple M3 Pro
